requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

findings.claim:
The new helper `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` still indexes `property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` without a guard. Its XML doc says it returns null for metadata properties, but it throws `IndexOutOfRangeException` instead. It also hard-casts to `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, which fails for positional record properties.

Concrete input: a `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T>` in a referenced assembly with `[Key((string)null)] public string Key { get; set; }`, used as `Item<int>` from a `[MessagePackObject]` type in the app. `CollectGeneric` runs `GetObjectInfo` on the metadata type and reaches the `intKey == null && stringKey == null` branch. In analyzer mode `reportDiagnostic` is non-null, so the `Invoke` argument is evaluated and the helper throws before `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` can drop the diagnostic. The result is AD0001, the same crash this requirement is meant to remove.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericStructNullKeyAnalyzerTests.AnalyzerDoesNotThrowOnMetadataGenericStructWithNullKey. It compiles the lib to a metadata reference, then runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer over the app compilation through CompilationWithAnalyzers with an onAnalyzerException hook. It expects zero analyzer exceptions and no AD0001; on head it captures an IndexOutOfRangeException. Rewriting the helper to use `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` makes it pass.

hunches.claim: The new wrapper now drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source in this compilation. That includes `Location.None`, which results whenever helpers such as `GetIdentifierLocation`, `GetLocation(IParameterSymbol)` or `GetParameterListLocation` return null for types declared in the compiling assembly. Before the change those diagnostics were still reported (without location); now real errors on in-assembly types can silently disappear. This contradicts 'types declared in the same assembly keep working as before'.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the full tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests suite on head. Any existing analyzer test that expects a MsgPack diagnostic without a source span (or a span the helpers fail to compute) fails because the diagnostic is no longer reported. Then add a mutant restoring `this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic;` and confirm that only metadata-located diagnostics differ.

hunches.claim: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] unguarded and casts to PropertyDeclarationSyntax, despite its doc saying it returns null for metadata. For a metadata property on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (e.g. a member of Item<T> with neither a Key nor an IgnoreMember), it throws IndexOutOfRangeException. The helper only moved the crash, so the reported bug remains for this path. It also can throw InvalidCastException for non-property-declaration syntax such as positional record parameters.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer/generator on the repro with lib compiled to a metadata reference, where Item<T> has a property with Key(null) or a null string key. Assert no AD0001/CS8785. Alternatively, replace [0] with FirstOrDefault and see whether the test still fails. Also try a positional record struct, whose properties come from a ParameterSyntax.

hunches.claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not an in-source location in this compilation. Diagnostics created with a null location (e.g. Diagnostic.Create(..., (Location?)null)) have Location.None and are now suppressed. Previously, users' builds could see these for source types. Location.None diagnostics (e.g. from MemberNeedsKey with a null location) or ones located in another syntax tree/partial declarations would no longer be reported, which changes diagnostics and could hide MsgPack errors users relied on.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005 etc.) plus a case with the type in a partial declaration or a diagnostic with a None location. Check that each expected diagnostic is still reported, comparing results with base and head.

hunches.claim: The new helper GetPropertyIdentifierLocation still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] unguarded, although its doc comment says it returns null for metadata properties. For a property on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path would still throw IndexOutOfRangeException, so the crash is not fixed there. The analyzer or generator exception also aborts collection, which can disable generated resolver output. This is a robustness and availability gap, not a deserialization-safety regression.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator/analyzer test where a referenced-assembly closed generic struct has a [Key]-less-valued property (Key attribute with null int and string key) and assert that no exception is thrown. Use FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() with a safe cast and re-run to confirm.

hunches.claim: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation is documented as returning null for metadata properties, but it still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] and casts to PropertyDeclarationSyntax. It will throw IndexOutOfRangeException for a metadata property. It also throws InvalidCastException for a record primary-constructor property, whose syntax is a ParameterSyntax. The helper does not follow the FirstOrDefault convention of its neighbouring helpers, and its doc comment is inaccurate.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test where a metadata-referenced closed generic struct has a property with no Key or IgnoreMember attribute and no int or string key. Run the generator and analyzer, and expect an IndexOutOfRangeException from GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. Alternatively, mutate [0] to FirstOrDefault()? and check that the test still passes.

hunches.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper in the constructor drops every diagnostic that has no in-compilation source location. A diagnostic created with a null location is Location.None and is silently dropped. Previously it would have been reported.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests for MsgPack003, MsgPack004 and MsgPack005. Confirm that none of them depend on a location-less diagnostic. Add a test that expects a diagnostic on a type with a null identifier location.

hunches.claim: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] and casts unguarded, even though its doc comment says it returns null for metadata. For a metadata property the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path would still throw IndexOutOfRangeException, so the helper does not fix that site. No test reaches this line, because the Key attributes in the tests are all valid.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1433 remove-guard: DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] -> DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault() (null-safe) or the reverse; expected to survive because no test makes a metadata closed generic with a [Key] whose int and string key are both null, so the line never runs for a metadata property. Add a test for it.

hunches.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper filters every reported diagnostic, but no test in the diff checks that diagnostics for in-compilation source types still reach the analyzer. The new tests only expect no diagnostics, so a mutant that always drops them (condition negated, or the body deleted) would pass. Existing analyzer tests may kill it, but nothing in this diff does.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1444 negate-condition: if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && ContainsSyntaxTree(...)) -> if (!(...)); expected to survive in the new tests because they all assert zero diagnostics. Run the new tests against the mutant.

hunches.claim: The 'UnkeyedMember' test claims to cover the MemberNeedsKey FirstOrDefault change at line 1077. The wrapper filter drops the diagnostic anyway, and the type is probably skipped before that line for a metadata type. The test would likely pass with the FirstOrDefault change reverted, so it does not isolate that fix. It also uses a non-record generic struct, so the Location argument may never be evaluated.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1077 delete-statement: revert FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() to DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation(); check whether ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember still passes. If it does, the mutant survives.

hunches.claim: The test helper runs the generator through a second manual CSharpGeneratorDriver. The main VerifyCS run skips the generated-sources check. The resolver-exists check therefore depends on that manual run, and it only looks at the hint name, not the generated content. A resolver that lacks the formatter for the closed generic struct would still pass.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the generator so the resolver omits the closed generic struct formatter while still emitting the file; Assert.Contains on the hint name still passes. Expect the mutant to survive.

hunches.claim: The README section says that generic value types can be used. It is a new docs section with no ledger backing, and the root cause is not fixed at its source. GetObjectInfo still runs on metadata closed generics, and diagnostics are only filtered afterwards, so there is no guard against the non-diagnostic crash paths.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the closed-generic branch of CollectGeneric in TypeCollector.cs. It calls GetObjectInfo on a metadata symbol. Check for other DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] uses that were not guarded.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: This is consistent with the recorded decision that referenced-assembly types are deliberately not analysed and that the defining assembly owns diagnostics. The new filter that drops diagnostics for metadata types and the docs describing it fit [L8].)
